clue.text: Laurel and Hardy started work with English vehicle

parts.note: Stan Laurel, the thin half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy

indicators.note: started signals that only the opening letter of the name Hardy is taken

parts.note: OP is the usual abbreviation for opus, a work

explanation.surface: The comic duo Laurel and Hardy begin a job involving an English car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laurel and Hardy' reads as one double act, but each name does its own job: Laurel gives his first name, Hardy only his initial.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light open horse-drawn carriage, an old-fashioned vehicle named after its first maker's patron.

clue.text: Old house on South London square

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed after, so the other pieces follow the first

explanation.surface: An ancient home sits on a square in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho Square is a garden square in London's West End, in the Soho district.

clue.text: Particular ambience found in restaurant

indicators.note: found in means the word is concealed inside the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A distinctive atmosphere is found in an eating place.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is the distinctive atmosphere or feeling surrounding a person or place.

clue.text: Not all the directors accepted hotel regime

parts.note: half is less than all
a company's directors form the board

explanation.surface: Only part of the management agreed to the hotel's rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted' is just a link between wordplay and definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel arrangement providing bed, breakfast and one main meal is a hotel regime of this kind.

clue.text: Regulators of the money one may draw out

definitions.text: Regulators of the money one may draw out

parts.words: Regulators of the money one may draw out
parts.note: the cords that pull a money bag shut, drawn tight or loosened, and figuratively control over spending

explanation.definitionFit: The cords of a money bag control access to it, so whoever holds them controls spending.

clue.text: Note serviceman boarding takes traditional meal

indicators.note: boarding means getting on and so going inside, here inside the word for takes

parts.note: takes means has, as in has a meal
G is a musical note
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier going aboard takes a classic dish with him.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is the traditional Scottish dish of offal and oatmeal, served on Burns Night.

clue.text: Single plane bearing A-bomb rises sadly?

indicators.note: in a down clue rises means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: the Enola Gay was the bomber that dropped the atomic bomb on Hiroshima

explanation.surface: A lone aircraft carrying an atomic bomb climbs, a sorrowful sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly?' is a joke: the plane was the Enola Gay, and the opposite of gay is sad, so only ENOLA remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To be alone is to be single, by oneself, without a companion.

clue.text: Current bore abandoned — a set-up for oil producers

indicators.note: abandoned means the word for bore is left out of the current

parts.note: the Gulf Stream is the warm Atlantic ocean current
to ream is to bore or widen a hole

indicators.note: up suggests the letters are disturbed and set in new order

explanation.surface: An ocean current and a dull person are left behind in a plan for oil-producing nations.
explanation.walkthrough: GULF STREAM loses REAM, and 'up' rearranges A SET to ATES.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf States are the oil-rich countries bordering the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Throngs swarming over ancient castle

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above the next piece
swarming suggests a crowd moving about, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: old means ancient

explanation.surface: Crowds pour across an old castle.
explanation.definitionFit: A stronghold is a fortified place, such as a castle or fortress.

clue.text: In which charges may be imposed to cover achievement

definitions.text: In which charges may be imposed to cover achievement

parts.words: In which charges may be imposed to cover achievement
parts.note: in the language of coats of arms a charge is a figure placed on a shield, and an achievement is the full armorial display

explanation.surface: Fees are levied to pay for some accomplishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests money charged to fund a success; 'charges' and 'achievement' are both technical terms from the art of coats of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: The study and design of coats of arms is the field where shields carry charges and the complete display is called an achievement.

clue.text: One who can deliver hat

definitions.meaning: in cricket the player who delivers the ball to the batsman
a hard felt hat with a rounded crown, the derby

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the cricketer who delivers the ball and a round hard felt hat.

clue.text: What can cause upset to flesh at toe?

definitions.text: What can cause upset to flesh at toe?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and so put in a different order

explanation.surface: Which ailment can trouble the skin between your toes?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: an ailment that troubles the skin of the toes.
explanation.definitionFit: This common fungal infection irritates the skin between the toes, so it is what upsets flesh there.

clue.text: What may be striking protest —- not as much working

parts.note: to object is to protest
less means not as much
on means working or operating, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A demonstration on strike means less work gets done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' suggests industrial action, but the definition means an example that strikes home, a vivid lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A vivid practical example that teaches by demonstration is something that may strike the learner forcibly.

clue.text: What children may achieve by putting heads together

definitions.text: What children may achieve by putting heads together

parts.words: What children may achieve by putting heads together
parts.note: children make a garland by threading the flower heads of small meadow blooms through each other's stems

explanation.definitionFit: Children make this garland by linking the flower heads of small lawn flowers, one through the next.

clue.text: Small contribution from upcoming girl in what's wildly successful hit

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word

parts.note: a wow is a great success

indicators.note: in a down clue upcoming means read from the bottom up

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
to smite is to hit

explanation.surface: A small donation from a rising young woman in a smash hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' (read upwards in a down clue) turns the girl's name before it goes inside; the widow's mite is the Gospel story of a poor woman's tiny gift.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospels a poor widow gives two tiny coins, so the phrase means a small but sincere contribution.

clue.text: Blair's book half concealed the female aspect of personality

indicators.note: half of the title is hidden away, leaving only its first five letters showing

parts.note: Eric Blair wrote under the name George Orwell, author of the novel Animal Farm

explanation.surface: Half of a prime minister's memoir conceals his feminine side.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair is not Tony but Eric Blair, the real name of George Orwell; his ten-letter title Animal Farm loses its second half.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jung's psychology the anima is the feminine side of a man's unconscious personality.

clue.text: A scoreboard could be great help when playing

indicators.note: when playing suggests the letters are in play and being moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: During a match a scoreboard might be very useful.
explanation.walkthrough: At cricket grounds the simple board showing the score is traditionally called a telegraph.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegraph board is the cricket name for a simple scoreboard displaying runs and wickets.

clue.text: Unfaithful queen at no time going over the line 'in deceit

indicators.note: going over means taking the place of, covering up the letter for line

parts.note: guile means deceit or cunning
L is the abbreviation for line
never means at no time

explanation.surface: A faithless queen never strays over the line of deception.
explanation.walkthrough: In GUILE the L is replaced by NEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's wife in the legends betrayed him through her love affair with Lancelot.

clue.text: Midwinter may show one such a writer's intention

parts.note: C. P. Snow was an English novelist
drift means meaning or intention, as in get my drift

explanation.surface: In the depths of winter an author's purpose may become clear.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is C. P. Snow, English author of Strangers and Brothers; his drift is what he means.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of wind-blown snow is a typical sight in the middle of winter, so the italic phrase describes one by example.

clue.text: Fish taken with a line is superb specimen

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, also called the orfe

explanation.surface: A fish caught on a line is a fine example.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect example of its kind, a model to aim at, is a superb specimen.

clue.text: Resist charge when operating money machine

indicators.note: operating suggests the letters are being worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Refuse an accusation when running a cash machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop till that records sales and holds the takings is a machine for money.

clue.text: One who won't comply 'concerning amount of -noise

parts.note: re means concerning, about
a bel is a unit of sound level, ten decibels

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to obey rules about how loud things may be.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebel is someone who resists authority and refuses to obey.

clue.text: Outlaw drug that's 'a 'cause 'of distress

parts.note: to ban is to outlaw
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Prohibit a narcotic that brings misery.
explanation.definitionFit: A bane is something causing ruin or great distress, as in the bane of my life.

clue.text: Duck cutting toe-nails, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters are taken

explanation.surface: A duck pecks at someone's toenails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' is just a link: take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater duck.

clue.text: With hands on hips try holding head on knees with body half showing

indicators.note: holding means one word contains the other

parts.note: to aim is to try or attempt

indicators.note: the head of knees is its first letter
only the first half of the word body is visible

explanation.surface: Attempt a pose, hands on hips, kneeling with half your body on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing akimbo means with hands on hips and elbows turned outwards.

clue.text: Constant excess level of press attention

parts.note: C is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
an overage is a surplus or excess amount

explanation.surface: There is a steady excessive amount of media interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Media coverage is the amount of reporting a story receives in newspapers and broadcasts.

clue.text: Pointer on dial showing peak

definitions.meaning: the moving indicator on a gauge or compass
a sharp pointed rock or summit

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the thin indicator on a gauge and a sharply pointed rock pinnacle.

clue.text: Light ale's flowing over yonder

indicators.note: over means lying across and so covering the other piece, which sits inside
flowing suggests liquid moving freely, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the beer word, with the possessive giving no letter
yonder means there, over that way

explanation.surface: A beer flows over there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective for the beer, but it is the definition; 'flowing' rearranges the beer and 'over' wraps the result around yonder's synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicate and airy, extremely light in weight or texture.
